facts.statement: One roll condition requires three dice, where the values of the first two dice added together must equal the value of the third die.
facts.sourceSentence: 3 dice required. 1st die + 2nd die must = the value of the third die. (i.e. 2+4=6)

facts.statement: The rules give 2+4=6 as an illustrative example of satisfying the addition roll condition.
facts.sourceSentence: 3 dice required. 1st die + 2nd die must = the value of the third die. (i.e. 2+4=6)

facts.statement: The addition roll condition is shown by a symbol pairing two unspecified die faces with a plus sign and an equals sign to a third unspecified die face.
One roll condition requires three dice that must all show sixes.
facts.sourceSentence: 3 dice required. They must all be sixes.

facts.statement: The all-sixes roll condition is shown by a symbol of three six-pip die faces.
One roll condition requires two dice that must show doubles (matching values).
facts.sourceSentence: 2 dice required. They must be doubles.

facts.statement: The doubles roll condition is shown by a symbol of two unspecified die faces joined by an equals sign.
One roll condition requires a single die that must show either a 2 or a 3.
facts.sourceSentence: 1 die required. It can be either a 2 or a 3 value.

facts.statement: The either-or roll condition is shown by two die faces separated by a slash.
facts.sourceSentence: Symbol shown: [ 2 ] / [ 3 ]  (a two-pip face and a three-pip face separated by a slash)

facts.statement: One roll condition requires two dice, where one die must show a 3 and the other must show a value greater than 3.
facts.sourceSentence: 2 dice required. One must be a 3, another greater than 3.

facts.statement: The greater-than roll condition is shown by an unspecified die face, a greater-than sign, and a three-pip die face.
facts.sourceSentence: Symbol shown: [ ? ] > [ 3 ]  (a "?" die, a greater-than sign, and a three-pip die face)

facts.statement: One roll condition requires two dice showing specifically a 4 and a 5.
facts.sourceSentence: 2 dice required. They must be a 4 and a 5.

facts.statement: The specific-pair roll condition is shown by a four-pip die face and a five-pip die face.
facts.sourceSentence: Symbol shown: [ 4 ] + [ 5 ]  (a four-pip face and a five-pip face)

facts.statement: A question-mark die face in a roll-condition symbol denotes a die whose specific value is not fixed by the symbol.
facts.sourceSentence: Symbol shown: [ ? ] > [ 3 ]  (a "?" die, a greater-than sign, and a three-pip die face)

facts.statement: Roll-condition symbols use the operator signs plus, equals, slash, and greater-than.
facts.sourceSentence: each example is a black-bordered yellow tile containing white/dark die-face glyphs and operator symbols (+, =, /, >)

facts.statement: Each roll-condition example is presented as a black-bordered yellow tile containing white/dark die-face glyphs.
facts.sourceSentence: each example is a black-bordered yellow tile containing white/dark die-face glyphs and operator symbols (+, =, /, >)

facts.statement: These example tiles use the same design as the roll-condition tiles printed on machine part cards.
facts.sourceSentence: matching the roll-condition tiles printed on machine part cards.
